claims.text: Phase-field modeling can enhance phase stability in material systems.
Phase-field modeling can refine microstructures in material systems.
The unspecified initial material system may exhibit phase instability.
The unspecified initial material system may have a suboptimal microstructure.
Phase-field models can predict microstructural features.
Phase-field modeling permits simulation of phase transformations under varying conditions.
Phase-field modeling permits simulation of microstructural evolution under varying conditions.
Simulating phase transformations and microstructural evolution with phase-field modeling leads to optimized material properties.
Applying phase-field modeling will improve phase stability.
Applying phase-field modeling will produce a refined microstructure.
Improved phase stability and microstructure refinement will enhance material properties.
The results of phase-field modeling vary with the material system.
The results depend on the accuracy of the phase-field model.
The effectiveness of phase-field modeling depends on the complexity of the material system.
The effectiveness of phase-field modeling depends on the selected simulation parameters.

contradictions.description: The intervention is defined as computational modeling, but the experiment treats materials as being physically processed 'with and without' phase-field modeling. No model-guided processing action is specified that could directly alter the material, so the physical improvement and proposed control comparison are inconsistent with the stated computational intervention.
